artifacts.summary: 3-phase plan: flock C1's two lake builds on the guard's published lock path, prove the race closed under repeated real concurrency, create nolints-style.txt and reconcile the contradicted ci.yml comment.

memory_candidates.content: When a repository-owned script must serialize against a build guard that lives in a disposable, regenerated deploy tree (.claude/), do not probe for or call the guard. Take an flock() on the same lock path the guard publishes in its own header as a stable convention (<repo-root>/.lake/build-guard.lock). Advisory locks are keyed on the path, not on the binary that opened it, so mutual exclusion becomes an emergent property with zero coupling: no detection logic, no hardcoded reference into the deploy tree, and unchanged behavior in a clone with no agent system deployed. The two tempting alternatives are worse: probing for the guard couples a deliverable to a disposable artifact and leaves guard-less clones racing; refusing to run on detected concurrency converts transient, self-resolving contention into a hard red a reader must re-attribute against the commit log, which is exactly the gate property being repaired. Bounded waiting converts contention into a slower green instead.
